answer: Panel approvals are aggregated as a sparse threshold signature where the signer set is chosen by a public rule rather than by the candidate, so a candidate cannot hand-pick the jury that reviews it. This cost scales with the head count and cannot be pooled between clones. A farm cannot pick its own mirror, cannot satisfy the mesa with one branch, and cannot reuse the echo that chose last time: the mirror, the mesa and the echo are all outside its control. The signer set is chosen externally and rotates every epoch.
